title: Report of the 2022 High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development
executive_summary: The 2022 High-Level Political Forum on Sustainable Development, convened under the Economic and Social Council, focused on "Building back better from COVID-19 while advancing the full implementation of the 2030 Agenda." Key challenges identified include the COVID-19 pandemic, Ukraine conflict, climate change, energy and food insecurity, high debt, and inflation, which hinder Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) progress. The forum emphasized the need for global solidarity, increased financing, debt crisis resolution, and transformational policies, including strengthening One Health, social protection, and gender equality. Special attention was given to vulnerable countries, especially small island developing States, with calls for a multidimensional vulnerability index. The forum reviewed SDGs 4 (education), 5 (gender equality), 14 (oceans), 15 (terrestrial ecosystems), and 17 (partnerships), highlighting the role of science, technology, and innovation. Voluntary national reviews from 44 countries were presented. The forum adopted a ministerial declaration and set the stage for the 2023 SDG Summit to accelerate implementation and recovery efforts.
characteristics: The 2022 High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) focused on building back better from COVID-19 while advancing the full implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, reviewing Goals 4, 5, 14, 15, and 17 in depth.
Key challenges identified include COVID-19 impacts, Ukraine conflict, climate change, energy and food insecurity, high debt, inflation, and natural disasters, which hinder SDG progress.
The forum emphasized the need for global solidarity, increased financing, debt crisis resolution, transformational policies, and inclusive participation of women, youth, and vulnerable groups.
Discussions highlighted the importance of science, technology, innovation, digitalization, and effective global governance for sustainable development and climate action.
The forum included 44 voluntary national reviews, thematic panels, regional messages, and adoption of a ministerial declaration to renew commitment to the 2030 Agenda.
Participation involved 187 UN member states, UN entities, intergovernmental organizations, and major stakeholder groups, with extensive side events and exhibitions.
practical_applications: Implementation and scaling up of international and regional cooperation and development financing to support the full implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
Strengthening One Health and social protection systems as part of transformational policies to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.
Promotion of decent jobs and inclusive policies to leave no one behind, with a focus on vulnerable groups including women and youth.

Preparation and organization of the Transforming Education Summit to address barriers to achieving Goal 4, including innovative financing for education and digitalization efforts to close the digital divide.

Implementation of gender-responsive policies and budgeting to address gender inequalities exacerbated by COVID-19, including prioritizing decent work, equal pay, and increased participation of women in decision-making.
Acceleration of Goal 14 (oceans) implementation through partnerships, collaboration, and improved global ocean governance mechanisms following the second United Nations Ocean Conference.
Multi-stakeholder collaboration to address terrestrial ecosystem sustainability, biodiversity loss, and climate change, aligned with the post-2020 global biodiversity framework.

Pursuit of reforms in international finance, debt, and taxation architecture to assist developing countries with debt sustainability, including coordinated policies for debt financing, relief, restructuring, and sound debt management.

Mobilization of science, technology, and digital innovation through international cooperation, financing, and a science, technology and innovation road map to support sustainable development and close the digital divide.
Engagement of local authorities and communities in inclusive implementation of the 2030 Agenda, including voluntary local reviews and local-level actions.
Conduct of voluntary national reviews by countries to assess and report progress on Sustainable Development Goals, facilitating peer learning and accountability.

Organization of thematic discussions and interactive panels on topics such as financing crisis response, mobilizing science and technology, capacity development, and partnerships for sustainable development.

Focused discussions and initiatives addressing the needs of African countries, least developed countries, landlocked developing countries, and small island developing States, including ensuring equal access to vaccines and resources.
Promotion of public, private, and civil society partnerships and multi-stakeholder coalitions to mobilize resources and financing for development with a focus on societal and intergenerational value.
Preparation for the 2023 Sustainable Development Goals Summit and midterm review to renew commitment and accelerate implementation of the Goals.

kpi_list.kpi_text: Implementing the 2030 Agenda and achieving a more resilient world will require strong global solidarity, scaled-up international and regional cooperation, increased development financing and addressing the debt crisis.
kpi_list.target_description: Achieve strong global solidarity, scaled-up international and regional cooperation, increased development financing, and address the debt crisis to implement the 2030 Agenda
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of international cooperation frameworks, financing flows, and debt sustainability measures
kpi_list.responsible_entity: United Nations Member States, Economic and Social Council

kpi_list.kpi_text: Urgent action is needed to implement the commitments on climate change, including the Glasgow Climate Pact, to keep alive the prospects of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.
kpi_list.target_description: Limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels
kpi_list.measurement_method: Global temperature monitoring and climate reporting
kpi_list.responsible_entity: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Parties, Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: A multidimensional vulnerability index has the potential to recognize the specific situation of small island developing States and contribute to a more useful, efficient and effective allocation of global financial flows.
kpi_list.target_description: Develop and implement a multidimensional vulnerability index to better allocate global financial flows to small island developing States and other vulnerable countries
kpi_list.measurement_method: Development and adoption of the index and its use in financial allocation decisions
kpi_list.responsible_entity: United Nations, International Financial Institutions, Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: The forthcoming Transforming Education Summit will provide an opportunity to address what currently hinders the achievement of Goal 4, including identifying innovative financial means for education and taking action to accelerate the recovery of the sector from the effects of the pandemic.
kpi_list.metric_name: Education Sector Recovery and Financing Innovation
kpi_list.target_description: Identify innovative financial means and accelerate recovery of education sector post-pandemic to achieve inclusive and equitable quality education (Goal 4)
kpi_list.measurement_method: Summit outcomes, financing commitments, and education recovery indicators

kpi_list.kpi_text: In 2022, no country in the world has achieved gender equality. The 2030 Agenda cannot be attained without a central focus on women and girls, who continue to face multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination and injustice worldwide.
kpi_list.target_description: Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls by addressing discrimination and injustice
kpi_list.measurement_method: Gender equality indices, policy adoption, and implementation monitoring
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, UN Women, Civil Society

kpi_list.kpi_text: It is also essential to prioritize decent work and equal pay for women and increase women’s participation in politics, senior management and decision-making.
kpi_list.target_description: Prioritize decent work, equal pay for women, and increase women’s participation in politics and senior decision-making roles
kpi_list.measurement_method: Labor market statistics, gender pay gap reports, political representation data

kpi_list.kpi_text: The political declaration of the second United Nations Ocean Conference re-energized the commitment for action towards accelerated implementation of Goal 14 through partnerships and collaboration.
kpi_list.target_description: Accelerate implementation of Goal 14 (oceans, seas and marine resources) through partnerships and collaboration
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring of partnerships, policy implementation, and ocean health indicators
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, UN Ocean-related bodies, NGOs

kpi_list.kpi_text: The post-2020 global biodiversity framework must be ambitious and put the world on a path to recover from biodiversity loss, including through effective monitoring and delivery of means of implementation.
kpi_list.target_description: Adopt and implement an ambitious global biodiversity framework to halt and reverse biodiversity loss
kpi_list.measurement_method: Framework adoption, biodiversity indicators, implementation reports
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Convention on Biological Diversity Parties, Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: An increase in flows of public and private finance is needed to bridge the financing gap and deliver on the promises of the Sustainable Development Goals.
kpi_list.metric_name: Increase in Public and Private Finance for SDGs
kpi_list.target_description: Increase flows of public and private finance to bridge the SDG financing gap
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking of financial flows, investment reports, SDG financing gap analyses
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, International Financial Institutions, Private Sector

kpi_list.kpi_text: Reforms in the international finance, debt and taxation architecture must be urgently pursued, with all countries and stakeholders taking an active and equal role.
kpi_list.metric_name: International Finance, Debt and Taxation Reform
kpi_list.target_description: Pursue urgent reforms in international finance, debt, and taxation architecture with active participation of all countries and stakeholders
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption and implementation of reform measures, stakeholder engagement reports
kpi_list.responsible_entity: Member States, International Financial Institutions, Tax Authorities

sdg_alignment: SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

top_themes.name: Multilateralism
top_themes.justification: Multilateralism is central to the document as the High-Level Political Forum itself is convened under the auspices of the Economic and Social Council, emphasizing global solidarity, international cooperation, and collective action to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The report repeatedly stresses the need for renewed multilateral action to address global challenges such as COVID-19, climate change, debt crises, and food insecurity, making this theme the most strategically important and extensively covered.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: Digital inclusion is highlighted as a priority area, especially in the context of education, closing the digital divide, and ensuring equal access to quality education and services. The document links digital inclusion to social protection, leaving no one behind, and empowering vulnerable groups, which aligns closely with the SDGs' core commitments to equity and social development.

top_themes.name: Digital Acceleration
top_themes.justification: Digital acceleration, including the role of science, technology, and innovation in sustainable development, is recognized as a critical enabler for recovery and progress towards the SDGs. The document discusses the importance of international cooperation in technology deployment and digital literacy, though this theme is less central than multilateralism and digital inclusion but still strategically important.
